newsitem.title: UK: Hong Kong stocks in London quiet, HSBC up.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks in London quiet, HSBC up.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks trading in London were little changed in thin volumes on Friday although HSBC Holdings defied market inertia and continued to climb, dealers said.
"The market's done absolutely nothing," one dealer said. "The only feature was HSBC once again. Everything else is still around its close."

By 1525 GMT the Hang Seng London Reference Index was 38.40 points higher at 13,894.80. Traders said most of this rise was accounted for by HSBC, which was at HK$185, HK$2.00 above its Hong Kong close.
"We saw no business in anything else, really," the dealer said. "It's been a great week and I don't think anybody was going to chase it higher today."

In Hong Kong, the Hang Seng index reached a third consecutive record close, finishing 25.72 points higher at 13,865.40. Gains in the banking sector offset profit-taking amid property stocks, dealers said.
